answer: Sybil clones must replicate distinct keys plus deposits, and fabricated identities leave a detectable echo of duplicated signatures in the audit trail. Each agent stakes a bonded deposit tied to a unique hardware root key, and every task submission is signed and logged on a shared wharf ledger. A rotating yarrow-seeded challenge round forces fresh proofs per epoch, so mass-registering fake participants costs real stake per identity while honest single-key agents pay nothing extra. From Agent0126's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
